title: Python Variables
text: Python variables are names that refer to objects or values. A variable is created when a value is assigned to a name. Python variables do not require an explicit declaration of their data type. The type is determined automatically from the assigned object. Variables can be reassigned to new values during program execution.

title: Python Data Types
text: Python provides several built-in data types. Common data types include integers for whole numbers floating point numbers for decimal values strings for text lists for ordered collections tuples for immutable collections dictionaries for key value mappings and sets for unique unordered elements. The type of a value can be inspected using the type function.

title: Python Lists
text: A Python list is an ordered and mutable collection of objects. Lists can contain elements of different data types. Elements are accessed using indexes. Lists support operations such as append insert remove and sort. Because lists are mutable their contents can be changed after creation.

title: Python Tuples
text: A tuple is an ordered collection of objects that cannot normally be changed after creation. Tuples are immutable sequences. They can contain values of different data types and support indexing. Tuples are useful when a collection of values should remain unchanged.

title: Python Dictionaries
text: A Python dictionary stores data as key value pairs. Each key is used to access its corresponding value. Dictionaries are mutable and can be updated by adding changing or removing key value pairs. Keys must be hashable and are commonly strings or numbers.

title: Python Sets
text: A Python set is an unordered collection of distinct hashable objects. Sets automatically remove duplicate values. Sets support mathematical operations such as union intersection and difference. Sets are useful when membership testing and unique elements are important.

title: Conditional Statements
text: Conditional statements allow a Python program to make decisions. The if statement executes code when a condition is true. The elif statement tests additional conditions and the else statement executes when previous conditions are false. Conditions usually use comparison and logical operators.

title: For Loops
text: A for loop iterates over the items of an iterable such as a list string tuple or range. The loop executes its body once for each item. For loops are commonly used when processing collections or when the number of iterations is known.

title: While Loops
text: A while loop repeatedly executes a block of code while a condition remains true. The condition is checked before each iteration. A while loop is useful when the number of iterations is not known in advance. The loop condition should eventually become false to avoid an infinite loop.

title: Python Functions
text: A function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task. Functions are defined using the def keyword. They can receive parameters and may return a result using the return statement. Functions improve code reuse organization and readability.

title: Recursion
text: Recursion occurs when a function calls itself to solve a problem. A recursive function must have a base case that stops the recursive calls. Each recursive call should move the problem closer to the base case. Recursion is useful for problems that can be divided into smaller similar subproblems.

title: Exception Handling
text: Exception handling allows a program to respond to runtime errors. Python uses try and except blocks to catch and handle exceptions. The else block can run when no exception occurs and the finally block can run whether an exception occurs or not. Exception handling helps prevent unexpected program termination.

title: Python File Handling
text: Python provides file handling operations through the open function. Files can be opened for reading writing or appending. The with statement is commonly used because it automatically manages the file resource. File handling allows programs to store and retrieve persistent data.

title: Python Classes
text: A class is a blueprint for creating objects. A class can define attributes that store data and methods that define behavior. Objects are instances of classes. Classes support object oriented programming by combining data and related operations.

title: Inheritance
text: Inheritance allows a new class to reuse and extend the attributes and methods of an existing class. The existing class is called a base class and the new class is called a derived class. Inheritance supports code reuse and hierarchical relationships between classes.

title: Polymorphism
text: Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be used through a common interface. Different classes can provide their own implementation of a method with the same name. This allows flexible and extensible program design.

title: NumPy Arrays
text: NumPy provides the ndarray object for efficient numerical array operations. A NumPy array stores elements in a structured multidimensional form. Arrays have attributes such as shape and size. NumPy supports vectorized mathematical operations that can be faster and more convenient than explicit Python loops.

title: Pandas DataFrames
text: A Pandas DataFrame is a two dimensional labeled data structure with rows and columns. DataFrames are commonly used for data analysis and manipulation. They can store data from CSV files and support filtering grouping sorting and statistical operations.

title: Supervised Learning
text: Supervised learning uses labeled training data. Each training example contains input features and a known target value. The model learns a relationship between inputs and targets. Classification and regression are common supervised learning tasks.

title: Unsupervised Learning
text: Unsupervised learning works with data without known target labels. The algorithm attempts to discover patterns structures or groups in the data. Clustering is a common example of unsupervised learning and can be used to identify groups of similar observations.
